## SA observes the 96th anniversary of Armistice Army Day

By CO Marumo Machete, S03 External Communication SA Army Photos by Lance Bombardier

Refilwe Sebopa

emories of Armistice of 96 years ago M were relived at the SA Army Headquarters in Pretoria as the Chief of the SA Army, Lt Gen Vusi Masondo; led the SA in marking International Remembrance Day Army Day.

Continuing a commemorative tradition that spans more than nine decades, a salvo from the Artillery's G1 gun opened the proceedings with deafening bang for the sombre remembrance of the survivors and those that laid down their lives during the war that lasted four from 1914 until the armistice in 1918. years

two-minute silence was observed, a minute for the survivors of the carnage of World War I and another for those who the ultimate sacrifice and perished the war. This culminated in the last salvo fired by the GI gun. paid during

The Chief of the SA laid wreath at the memorial on the lawns of the SA Headquarters complex before delivering his tribute: Army Army

Addressing the Army Council and the Generals and spectators in attendance; Lt Gen Masondo those in attendance never to take for granted the selfless sacrifices made by those who were involved in the war urged

Lt Gen Masondo said: "As the SA marches into its third decade of defending our democracy, let us join the world as it pauses to reflect Army and remember the warriors of the Great War:"

ABOVE: Lt Gen Vusi Masondo; the Chief of the SA laid a wreath at the memorial on the lawns of the SA Headquarters complex before delivering his tribute. Army, Army

continued: "Let us honour their sacrifice and strive for a peaceful world where no innocent blood will have to be spilled, as there are so many forms of recourse to avert war and prevent conflict from escalating He also homage He paid to the South African soldiers who died pursuing peace and stability on the African continent following the country's post-1994 readmission to the international community.
